question.problem:
The random variable $X$ represents the age of a randomly selected child from a football team, and the random variable $Y$ represents the age of a randomly selected child from a baseball team. The probability distributions of $X$ and $Y$ are given below.
$x$ $10$ $11$ $12$ $13$
$f(x)$ $0.1$ $0.2$ $0.35$ $0.35$
$y$ $10$ $11$ $12$
$f(y)$ $0.2$ $0.25$ $0.55$

One child is selected at random from each team. Calculate the expected sum of ages of the two children.
question.worked_solution:
We need to calculate $\text{E}[X+Y].$

Recall that if $X$ and $Y$ are random variables (not necessarily independent), and $a$ and $b$ are constants, then

$$
\text{E}[aX+bY]=a\text{E}[X]+b\text{E}[Y].
$$

The expected values of $X$ and $Y$ are calculated as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =10\cdot 0.1+11\cdot 0.2+12\cdot 0.35+13\cdot 0.35=11.95 \\ \text{E}[Y] & =10\cdot 0.2+11\cdot 0.25+12\cdot 0.55=11.35\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we get

$$
\text{E}[X+Y]=\text{E}[X]+\text{E}[Y]=11.95+11.35=23.3.
$$
